summary.short: Iowa law sets rules for automated driving systems and driverless-capable vehicles on public highways. Permits driverless operation when vehicles meet minimal-risk, traffic-law and federal certification conditions; requires owners to hold liability insurance and report accidents; allows on-demand driverless networks; centralizes regulation in the state department and bars local rules and taxes.
summary.long: The Act adds new sections 321.514 to 321.519 on automated driving systems (ADS) and system-equipped vehicles. Section 321.514 defines terms including ADS, driverless-capable vehicle, minimal risk condition, operational design domain and on-demand driverless-capable vehicle network. Section 321.515 lets a driverless-capable vehicle operate on public highways without a human driver if it can reach a minimal risk condition after an ADS malfunction, can comply with state traffic and safety laws (unless the department grants an exemption), and is certified by its manufacturer as compliant with federal motor vehicle safety standards. Operation with a human driver present is lawful if the driver holds a valid license, is subject to the liability coverage and penalties of section 321.20B and regains manual control when prompted. Section 321.516 requires owners to obtain financial liability coverage before operating a system-equipped vehicle. Section 321.517 requires such vehicles to remain at the scene of an accident and requires the owner to report it to law enforcement; non-compliance is imputed to the owner, who may be charged and convicted. Section 321.518 allows on-demand driverless-capable vehicle networks. Section 321.519 places these vehicles under the department, which may adopt rules under chapter 17A, and bars political subdivisions from imposing additional requirements or vehicle-specific taxes.

evidence.quote: “Automated driving system” means the hardware and software collectively capable of performing the entire dynamic driving task on a sustained basis, regardless of whether the system is limited to a specific operational design domain, if any.

“Conventional human driver” means a natural person who manually controls the in-vehicle accelerating, braking, steering, and transmission gear selection input devices in order to operate a motor vehicle.

definitions.term: driverless-capable vehicle (printed as 'Driver less-capable vehicle'; operative provisions use 'driverless-capable vehicle')

evidence.quote: ''Driver less-capable vehicle" means a system-equipped vehicle capable of performing the entire dynamic driving task within the automated driving system's operational design domain, if any, including but not limited to achievement of a minimal risk condition without intervention or supervision by a conventional human driver.

“Dynamic driving task” means all real-time operational and tactical functions required to operate a motor vehicle on a highway in traffic within an automated driving system's specific operational design domain, if any.

Minimal risk condition” means a reasonably safe state to which an automated driving system brings a system-equipped vehicle upon experiencing a performance-relevant failure of the system that renders the system unable to perform the entire dynamic driving task
a transportation service network that uses a software application or other digital means to dispatch driverless-capable vehicles for the purposes of transporting persons or goods

“Operational design domain” means a set of constraints used to define the domain under which an automated driving system is designed to properly operate, including but not limited to types of highways, speed ranges, environmental conditions such as weather or time of day, and other constraints.
“System-equipped vehicle” means a motor vehicle equipped with an automated driving system.

obligations.summary: Driverless-capable vehicle may operate without a conventional human driver only if it meets listed conditions: capability to reach a minimal risk condition on system malfunction, capability to comply with state traffic and safety laws (unless exempted by the department), and manufacturer certification of compliance with federal motor vehicle safety standards (unless exempted).
